notes.heading: Background of Disaster Management in India
points: India is highly vulnerable to multiple types of disasters due to its geographical location and climatic conditions
About 60% of land is prone to earthquakes, and large areas face floods, cyclones, droughts, and landslides
Earlier disaster response in India was reactive rather than proactive
Relief work was mainly handled by revenue departments and ad-hoc committees
Major disasters like the 1999 Odisha cyclone and 2001 Gujarat earthquake highlighted the need for a structured system
Shift from relief-centric approach to risk reduction and preparedness approach

notes.heading: Evolution of Disaster Management System in India
points: Earlier framework focused only on post-disaster relief
Tenth Five Year Plan introduced structured disaster management planning
2001 Gujarat earthquake acted as a turning point
High-level committee recommended a national disaster management framework
Creation of dedicated institutions like NDMA and SDMAs

notes.heading: National Disaster Management Act, 2005 – Overview
points: Enacted to provide legal and institutional framework for disaster management in India
Came into force in December 2005
Established a systematic and proactive disaster management structure
Focus shifted from relief to preparedness, mitigation, and capacity building
Provides multi-level governance structure from national to district level

notes.heading: Key Institutional Structure under NDMA Act 2005
points: National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) – apex body headed by Prime Minister
State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) – headed by Chief Minister
District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) – headed by District Collector
National Executive Committee (NEC) – assists NDMA in implementation
National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) – specialized response force

notes.heading: Functions of NDMA
points: Laying down policies and guidelines for disaster management
Approving national disaster management plans
Coordinating enforcement of policies
Recommending funds for mitigation and preparedness
Promoting training, research, and awareness programs

notes.heading: State and District Level Functions
points: SDMAs prepare state disaster management plans
DDMAs implement disaster plans at district level
Local authorities are responsible for community-level preparedness
Coordination between central and state agencies is essential
Focus on decentralised disaster management

notes.heading: National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)
points: Specialized force created under NDMA Act 2005
Trained for search, rescue, and relief operations
Works under Ministry of Home Affairs
Deployed during major disasters like floods, earthquakes, cyclones
Acts as first responder during emergencies

notes.heading: Key Features of NDMA Act 2005
points: Legal framework for disaster management in India
Multi-tier institutional structure
Shift from relief-based to holistic disaster management
Emphasis on mitigation and preparedness
Integration of disaster management into development planning

notes.heading: National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), 2009
points: Formulated to create a holistic framework for disaster management in India
Shifted focus from reactive relief to proactive risk reduction
Emphasizes prevention, mitigation, preparedness, and response
Aims to build a safer and disaster-resilient India
Promotes community participation and capacity building

notes.heading: Key Features of NPDM 2009
points: Integration of disaster management with development planning
Emphasis on hazard risk assessment and vulnerability reduction
Strengthening institutional mechanisms like NDMA, SDMA, DDMA
Focus on early warning systems and forecasting
Encourages public-private partnership and community involvement

notes.heading: Objectives of NPDM 2009
points: Minimize loss of lives and property
Promote culture of prevention and preparedness
Build institutional and community resilience
Ensure efficient response mechanisms
Strengthen disaster risk reduction at all levels

notes.heading: National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP), 2016
points: First national plan aligned with Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction
Prepared by National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)
Provides detailed operational guidelines for disaster management
Focus on risk reduction and resilience building
Covers all types of disasters in a comprehensive manner

notes.heading: Key Features of NDMP 2016
points: Multi-hazard approach covering natural and man-made disasters
Four stages: prevention, mitigation, response, and recovery
Clear roles and responsibilities for all stakeholders
Emphasis on technology and data-driven disaster management
Integration with national development planning

notes.heading: Salient Components of NDMP 2016
points: Hazard risk assessment and vulnerability mapping
Preparedness and capacity building
Early warning systems and communication
Response and relief coordination
Rehabilitation and reconstruction strategies

notes.heading: Disaster Management Cycle in India
points: A continuous process to manage disasters systematically
Focus on reducing risk and improving resilience
Involves pre-disaster, during disaster, and post-disaster phases
Implemented through NDMA, SDMA, and DDMA
Aligned with national policies and plans like NPDM and NDMP

notes.heading: Phases of Disaster Management Cycle in India
points: Pre-disaster phase – mitigation, prevention, preparedness
During disaster phase – response, rescue, and relief operations
Post-disaster phase – rehabilitation and reconstruction
Recovery phase – restoring normal life and infrastructure
Learning and feedback for future risk reduction
